## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C IPO and TRA execution

- 2012-04-13: S-1/A No. 7 files the form-of TRA as Exhibit 10.4.
- 2012-05-02: IPO closes; executed Tax Receivable Agreement dated May 2, 2012 between Carlyle Holdings I GP Inc., Carlyle Holdings I L.P., The Carlyle Group L.P., and the Limited Partners.
- 2012-05-08: 8-K reports IPO close and files the executed TRA as Exhibit 10.2.

#### Conversion amendment

- 2020-01-01: Amendment effective at 12:02 a.m. ET; expanded recitals state that the L.P.-to-corporation Conversion is not an Exchange and that no further Exchanges will occur post-Conversion. Updates "Change of Control," "Continuing Director," "Exchange," and "LIBOR" definitions. 85% payment percentage and Section 754 attribute scope unchanged. Filed as Exhibit 99.2 to the January 2, 2020 8-K.

## Explanation

The TRA originates from Carlyle's May 2, 2012 Up-C IPO and obligated Carlyle Holdings I GP Inc. (the Corporate Taxpayer subsidiary) to pay 85% of cash tax savings on Section 754 basis step-ups from exchanges of Carlyle Holdings partnership units, plus imputed-interest deductions. The January 1, 2020 Amendment, executed in connection with Carlyle's conversion from a Delaware limited partnership to a Delaware corporation, closes the agreement to new Exchanges and converts it into a run-off: pre-Conversion basis step-ups continue to generate annual Tax Benefit Payments, but no new exchanges can add to the beneficiary pool. The $344M deferred consideration paid in five installments from 2020 through 2024 to former Carlyle Holdings unitholders is a separate obligation, not a TRA payment. The TRA carrying balance was $71.8M at December 31, 2025; a Delaware Chancery derivative action (Borenstein) challenges the 2020 amendment's effect but is litigation about its validity, not a separate contract modification. See `contract_log.md` for the same-contract analysis across the form-of, executed, and amendment versions.
